output.title: Acceptance walkthroughs as a workflow control
output.body:
If you are automating work in a small business, an acceptance walkthrough is not a nice extra. It is the step where the owner reviews the AI output before it can commit to money, a customer promise, or another downstream system. In plain terms: the model can suggest, but the owner still decides.

That matters most for an owner-operator who has tried ChatGPT but has not tied it into a real workflow yet. The question is not whether AI can produce an answer. The question is where human approval has to stay in place so the business keeps control. Bareni’s own self-built AP demo uses that boundary in a narrow way: amount-based human-only approval, duplicate blocking, refusal of agent approval/payment attempts, and audit records. It is synthetic-data demo work, not a customer deployment.

A practical next step is to pick one repeating workflow, such as invoice approval, customer replies, or lead qualification, and mark the exact point where review happens. Then test it against your current manual process. If the review point is clear and repeatable, bounded automation may fit. If every step needs hand-holding, the workflow is probably not ready. That is usually where the awkward truth lives.
